quickAnswer: In Norfolk, 95.4% of households own their home, 91.1% of housing units are single-family detached, and 62.8% of homes burn oil (ACS 2022). With so few rentals and so little gas, a replacement usually means oil versus a heat pump.
body: ## A town where almost everyone owns the house

In the Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS), Norfolk has 3,291 occupied homes, and 3,138 of them (95.4%) are owner-occupied. Only 153 households rent (4.6%), the lowest share of all 50 towns we serve, against 16.4% for the middle town. Single-family detached houses make up 3,107 of the 3,412 housing units (91.1%), 5th-highest of the 50, and no unit is a mobile home.

The rental heat rules in the State Sanitary Code touch a much smaller share of households here than in most of our towns. In an owner-occupied house, the owner generally makes the decisions about oil tanks, ducts and attic insulation. Multi-unit buildings are only 135 of the housing units (4.0%).
## Oil tanks and LP cylinders instead of gas lines

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 2,067 Norfolk homes, 62.8% of occupied homes and 7th-highest of the 50 towns, well above the 36.5% of the middle town. Bottled or tank (LP) gas heats 363 more (11.0%), 4th-highest. Utility gas serves 566 homes (17.2%), 44th of 50, and electricity heats 159 (4.8%), 49th of 50. Wood is the fuel for 52 homes.

A replacement here often begins with an existing oil boiler or furnace. The decision is often one of three: a new oil unit, a cold-climate heat pump with the old system as backup, or a full move to heat pumps. Gas conversion is possible only where a main reaches the street, and the gas company can confirm that. We assess the home's heating load before quoting, because oversized equipment can waste fuel and wear out sooner.
## Mostly built from 1960 on, with the biggest wave from 1980 to 1999

The median Norfolk home was built in 1982, seven years newer than the 1975 of the middle town. The largest group, 1,212 units (35.5%), went up between 1980 and 1999. Another 925 (27.1%) date from 1960 to 1979, and 426 (12.5%) from 1940 to 1959. Only 179 (5.2%) are from 1939 or earlier, 49th of 50, and 44.8% were built before 1980. At the newer end, 450 homes (13.2%) are from 2010 or later, 5th-highest.

A house from that wave may not have the problems of a pre-war one, but an original furnace or boiler of that age can be near the end of a normal service life. Newer houses are also generally tighter, which can make ventilation and correct sizing more important. The median home value is $649,800, against $579,150 for the middle town.
## Mills, a rail line and a prison: what Norfolk's record says about its growth

Norfolk sits on an upper valley of the Charles River and was part of Dedham, then of Wrentham, where it was known as North Wrentham. It separated and was incorporated as Norfolk in 1870. Villages formed around sawmills and gristmills in the 17th and 18th centuries, and three cotton manufacturing companies were established at Stony Brook after 1812. The Norfolk County Railroad opened in 1849.

Population rose rapidly after 1925, when a hospital and a state prison were built on the Walpole line. Major residential development took place before 1940 in the Pondville and Clark Streets section, with scattered new housing along Seekonk and Main Streets, and suburban building has continued since. Norfolk covers 15.2 square miles, of which 14.8 are land.
## Rebates and the electric utility

We cannot confirm Norfolk's electric utility from the data we hold. Mass Save heat pump rebates run through the utility that serves the address, so find out which one that is before you order equipment. The [heat pump page](/cities/norfolk/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the 2026 terms.

faq.q: Should I replace my Norfolk oil boiler with a heat pump?
faq.a: It depends on the house. With 62.8% of Norfolk homes on oil, this is a common choice. A heat pump can carry most of the load in a well-sealed house, and some owners keep the boiler for the coldest days. The heating load is assessed before a system is quoted.

faq.q: Is natural gas available on my Norfolk street?
faq.a: Only 17.2% of Norfolk homes use utility gas, so a main may not reach every street. The gas company can tell you whether one reaches your address, and the answer decides whether conversion is even an option. If not, oil, LP or a heat pump are the paths.

faq.q: My Norfolk house was built in the 1980s. Is the original system likely to be old?
faq.a: If it has never been replaced, it is more than three decades old, which is past the usual life of many boilers and furnaces. Age alone does not mean failure, but an annual tune-up can show how much life is left, and we can price a replacement ahead of a breakdown.

faq.q: Who pays for heat in the rare Norfolk rental?
faq.a: Unless the lease says otherwise, the landlord pays under the State Sanitary Code, which requires at least 68 F from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. and at least 64 F overnight during the heating season. This is general information, not legal advice. Rentals are only 4.6% of Norfolk households.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil and LP gas make up most Norfolk heating (ACS 2022), so a heating failure often involves a tank, a delivery arrangement and a decision about the next system. Utility gas reaches just 566 homes, 44th of the 50 towns.
body: ## When the boiler fails in an oil-and-LP town

A dead boiler in January leaves little time. In Norfolk the unit is far more likely to burn oil than gas, and the next question is whether to put in the same kind of system. Putting in another oil boiler or furnace is the least disruptive swap. A heat pump with the old unit kept as a backup is the middle path, and a full heat pump system is the biggest change.
### What matters in a replacement

- Fuel, tank location and tank condition. Oil tanks and LP cylinders both age.
- The distribution: hot-water baseboard, a forced-air duct system or radiators decide how easy a swap is.
- Venting and the chimney, which can need changes when equipment is more efficient.
- The heating load of the house, so the new unit is the right size.
### Houses from the 1982 median

The median Norfolk house was built in 1982. Original equipment in a house of that age, if it has never been replaced, may be close to the end of its life. Modern boilers and furnaces can also differ from the one they replace in size and venting. Oil heats 2,067 homes (62.8%) against 36.5% in the middle town, and LP gas heats 363 (11.0%), 4th of 50.
### If you do have gas

Gas serves 566 of the town's 3,291 occupied homes (17.2%). For those, a licensed plumber or gas fitter has to pull the permit, and the town's building department can say which inspection closes out the job.
### Renters

Norfolk has just 153 renter households (4.6%), the lowest share of the 50 towns. The State Sanitary Code still sets heat minimums for a rented unit in the heating season, 68 F by day and 64 F at night, and the landlord covers heat unless the lease says otherwise. General information, not legal advice.
### Emergencies

Call (508) 786-8755 day or night. Emergency calls are answered around the clock, and the free written estimate arrives before anything starts. For a move toward electric heat, read the [heat pump page](/cities/norfolk/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: How do I know if I should repair or replace?
faq.a: A fault in one part of a fairly young unit is usually worth repairing. A unit that is old, keeps needing service or has a cracked heat exchanger (a safety matter) is a candidate for replacement.

faq.q: Do you work on LP gas systems?
faq.a: Heating installation and repair is part of what Mass HVAC does for homes and businesses, and LP gas has the 4th-highest share among the 50 towns here. Tank connections, venting and permit steps depend on the equipment.

faq.q: Does the 1982 median year mean my boiler is old?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The median Norfolk home dates to 1982 (ACS 2022), but a boiler may have been replaced since. The unit's own age and condition matter more than the house's year, and a look at the nameplate tells us where it stands.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Detached houses are 91.1% of Norfolk's housing units (ACS 2022), so cooling often comes down to a choice between a ducted system and ductless heads. Sizing matters either way, and the electrical panel gets a look before anything is ordered.
body: ## Cooling detached houses: ducts, mini-splits or both

With 3,107 of Norfolk's housing units being single-family detached houses, there is generally more freedom than in an apartment building to place an outdoor unit and choose a layout. Attached townhouses are 170 units (5.0%), and the remaining multi-unit buildings are few, so the apartment-style cooling problem is rare.
### Ducted central air

Central air works best where the house has ductwork that is correctly sized and sealed. A forced-air house has ducts, but they may have been sized for heating, which is not always right for cooling. A house heated by hot-water baseboard often has no ducts at all.
### Ductless in a house with baseboard

In a house with a hot-water boiler, baseboard or radiators leave no ducts to reuse. A ductless mini-split puts an indoor head in each room or zone you want to cool, joined to an outdoor unit by a small line set. With the right model it also heats in the shoulder seasons.
### Newer and older halves of the town

Older houses, including the 179 built in 1939 or earlier, may have no duct space, which often points toward ductless. The largest age group runs from 1980 to 1999 (1,212 units, 35.5%), and what each of those houses contains varies, so the job can be a repair, a replacement or a better sized condenser.
### The electrical side
Only 159 Norfolk homes (4.8%) heat with electricity, 49th of 50. A large new cooling unit adds electrical load, so the panel's capacity should be checked before it is ordered.
### Humidity
A system that is too large cools quickly but shuts off before it removes moisture, leaving rooms cold and damp. Correct sizing, from the house itself, gives steadier temperatures.
### How the housing mix shapes the job

Norfolk ranks 5th of 50 for detached homes (91.1%), well above the 76.7% of the middle town. Buildings with 2 units number 53, those with 3 or 4 units number 28 and those with 5 or more number 54, so multi-unit buildings total only 135 (4.0%), 48th of 50. Cooling work here is mostly one house at a time, with its own layout and its own panel.

faq.q: Can I cool a Norfolk house that heats with baseboard?
faq.a: Yes. The indoor heads join the outdoor unit through a small line set, so no ducts are needed. We work out the capacity from the rooms involved and pick a place for the condenser.

faq.q: Should I replace central air and the furnace together?
faq.a: Sometimes. If both are old, a matched system can make sense. If only one is failing, it can often be replaced alone.

faq.q: Can one mini-split cool a whole Norfolk house?
faq.a: Sometimes, in a compact layout. Several rooms usually need several heads, or a multi-zone outdoor unit. The room count and the floor plan decide.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Norfolk burns oil in 62.8% of occupied homes and LP gas in 11.0%, so a heat pump is a natural comparison. Our data does not confirm the electric utility, and the rebate path depends on the utility that serves the address.
body: ## Where oil and LP set the baseline

Oil heats 2,067 Norfolk homes and LP gas heats 363, ranking 7th and 4th of the 50 towns. Pipeline gas serves 566 homes (17.2%) and electricity heats 159 (4.8%), 49th of 50, so for most households a heat pump would be the first electric heating system in the house. Cold-climate models are built for New England winters, and the electricity they use replaces part or all of the delivered fuel.
### Utility not confirmed

We have no confirmed electric utility for Norfolk, so nobody can say from here which program path a given address takes. Your electric bill names the company. The 2026 Mass Save whole-home rebate pays $2,650 per ton to a cap of $8,500, provided the house has been weatherized; our [heat pump overview](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) has the rest.
### The age bands against the weatherization test

Homes from 2000 on number 670 (19.6%), and 450 of them date from 2010 or later (13.2%, 5th of 50). The larger groups are older: 1,212 units from 1980 to 1999 (35.5%), 925 from 1960 to 1979 and 426 from 1940 to 1959. For those, the route usually begins with a Home Energy Assessment.
### Detached houses and what they leave room for

With 3,107 detached houses (91.1%), there is usually room for an outdoor unit. A house with hot-water baseboard can take ductless heads, and a forced-air house may use a ducted unit on the ducts it has. The 170 attached townhouses (5.0%) face tighter siting questions.
### Owners, value and the other fuels

Owners occupy 3,138 of the 3,291 occupied homes (95.4%), so an equipment decision usually belongs to the household that owns the house. The median value is $649,800 (20th of 50), and spending on a heating system is judged against that. The Census also lists 18 homes on solar and 66 on other fuel or coal, so not every Norfolk house fits the oil-or-LP picture.
### The boiler question

Some owners leave the oil boiler connected for the sharpest cold and let the heat pump run the rest of the year. The heating-load calculation decides whether that is needed. Our [heating page](/cities/norfolk/heating-installation-repair) covers a straight replacement.

faq.q: Which utility serves my Norfolk address?
faq.a: Your electric bill names it. Our data does not confirm it, and the rebate path depends on the utility serving the address, so check with Mass Save before signing.

faq.q: Is Norfolk's housing new enough for the weatherization shortcut?
faq.a: For about one home in five. The Census counts 670 of 3,412 units (19.6%) from 2000 or later. Everyone else would typically begin with an energy assessment.

faq.q: Can a heat pump handle the cooling too?
faq.a: Yes, it heats and cools, so one project can retire a failing air conditioner. We size from the heating load and confirm that the cooling need is covered.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil burners need a yearly cleaning, and 62.8% of Norfolk homes heat with oil (ACS 2022). Owners occupy 95.4% of households, so a tune-up is mostly a question for homeowners.
body: ## Tune-ups for owners who burn oil and LP

Regular maintenance can help avoid a breakdown. At the 2,067 oil homes, a visit means the burner is cleaned, the nozzle and filter are replaced and combustion is tested. For LP systems, it means checking the burner, venting and controls. For the gas, electric and heat pump minority, it means safety checks, coils and filters.
### Equipment from the 1980 to 1999 wave

The largest age band in town runs from 1980 to 1999, and equipment that dates from that period, if it has never been replaced, is now old. A tune-up can show whether a system has years left or is due for planned replacement, which beats a no-heat call at night.
### Who schedules the visit

Owners occupy 3,138 of 3,291 occupied homes (95.4%) and renters hold 153 (4.6%), the lowest renter share of the 50 towns. The schedule is mostly each household's own decision, which makes the yearly reminder an owner's habit rather than a lease term.
### LP and the smaller fuels
LP gas heats 363 homes (11.0%), 4th of 50. The Census also counts 52 homes on wood, 18 on solar and 66 on other fuel or coal. Each of those has its own venting and controls worth a yearly look.
### Fall visit, spring visit

- **September or October:** heating tune-up, before the cold nights.
- **April or May:** air conditioner or mini-split check, before the first hot week.
- **Any time:** a new noise, an oil smell, soot, short cycling or an unusually high bill is a reason to call.
### Owner tasks between visits

Between visits, clear leaves and snow from outdoor units, keep the burner area free of clutter and read the tank gauge now and then. LP customers should know where the tank shutoff is. Check thermostat settings and batteries before concluding a system has failed.
### Why not wait for a breakdown

Emergency work on a cold night can be more stressful and sometimes more expensive than a planned replacement. Mass HVAC takes emergency calls 24 hours a day, but a scheduled visit can keep you out of that position.
### What to have ready
The fuel, the age of the unit, the make and model if you can read them, and what you noticed. For cooling, see the [cooling page](/cities/norfolk/air-conditioning-installation-repair).

faq.q: How often should I service an oil boiler?
faq.a: Every year, ahead of the heating season. A skipped cleaning can leave soot behind and hurt both efficiency and reliability.

faq.q: Is a tune-up worth it on a newer system?
faq.a: Usually. Even new equipment has filters, drains and outdoor coils that clog, and a small problem found in the fall costs less than one found in January.

faq.q: Do the newest homes need a visit too?
faq.a: Yes. The 450 homes built since 2010 (13.2%) rank 5th of 50, and newer equipment still has filters, drains and outdoor coils. A first-year visit can confirm the system is running as it should.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Most Norfolk housing units date from 1960 on. For houses of that age, ventilation, humidity and filtration are the main air questions, along with oil and LP combustion safety.
body: ## Air in houses built mostly after 1960

Few Norfolk homes date from 1939 or earlier (179, or 5.2%, 49th of 50), while the bulk went up between 1960 and 1999, with 925 from 1960 to 1979 and 1,212 from 1980 to 1999. Houses of that age are often neither as leaky as the oldest stock nor as tight as the newest. Each has its own air questions. The town's history notes major residential development before 1940 in the Pondville and Clark Streets section, and houses from that era are where the older-materials caution is most likely to apply. Older houses also tend to leak more air, which thins some pollutants but lets in dust and damp.
### The tighter houses

Homes built in 2000 or later, and especially those since 2010, are generally tighter. In a tighter shell, cooking fumes and moisture linger unless a fan removes them. Of the fixes in a house like this, a bath fan ducted outdoors and a range hood are among the least expensive. In a detached house they can often vent straight through a nearby wall or roof, which is harder in a multi-unit building, and only 135 Norfolk units are in one.
### Combustion and carbon monoxide

Oil and LP burners produce combustion gases that should leave through the flue. Keep burners tuned, keep flues clear and have a working carbon monoxide alarm near sleeping areas. Wood heats 52 Norfolk homes, and a stove or fireplace also needs a clean chimney.
### Basements and humidity

Dry winter air and muggy summer air both show up indoors. In Norfolk 3,107 of the housing units are detached houses (91.1%), so each household manages its own moisture, and only 135 units sit in multi-unit buildings (4.0%), which makes shared walls a minor route for air to move between homes.  If a basement is damp, a dehumidifier helps, while the water getting in needs its own repair.
### Filters, ducts and fresh air

- Upgrade filtration and keep filters changed.
- Add a humidifier or dehumidifier tied to the system.
- Add or repair ventilation in a tight house.
- Clean ducts that are visibly dirty or damaged.
### Testing

A test of humidity, carbon monoxide or particles shows one moment in time, so correcting the source matters more than the reading. If an older house is going to be renovated, testing for older materials by a qualified specialist comes first.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Not automatically. Dirt, mold or damage inside the ducts is the reason to clean; without it, cleaning adds little. We inspect first.

faq.q: Should I have a carbon monoxide alarm with an oil or LP system?
faq.a: Yes. Any fuel-burning appliance warrants one near sleeping areas. It is a basic safety device and does not replace a yearly tune-up.

faq.q: Do wood stoves matter for air quality here?
faq.a: Wood is the main heat in 52 Norfolk homes. A stove or fireplace needs a clean chimney and dry wood, and a carbon monoxide alarm should be nearby.
